summary: All core payment inputs checked out against the primary CMS, BLS, TWC, IRS, TMHP, MedPAC, KFF and TAC sources: the CY 2026 national period ($2,038.22 / $1,998.41), 74.9% labor share, the Texas CBSA wage indexes (Houston 0.9729 etc., checked in the CMS file), LUPA per-visit amounts, the 7% LUPA share, $750 enrollment fee, $2,625 HCSSA fees, TMHP G0299/G0300 $98.92, every O*NET/OEWS 2025 wage, the 10/7-patient SOM rule, §489.28 50% non-borrowed, and the 26 TAC 558 / 42 CFR 484 requirements. The P&L arithmetic reproduces the narrative (hha100 about 7.5% margin, hha50_ffs break-even). Main problems: (1) the checklist and recommendations tell applicants to request only the LHHS category, but §558.13(d) requires requesting the licensed-and-certified category up front to get the interim license and automatic upgrade; (2) the default config's profit depends on an unsourced MA proxy ($173.37/visit; it breaks even at about $141); (3) the mandatory HHCAHPS vendor cost is missing; (4) hours per visit are unsourced and lean; (5) leadership salaries are statewide while revenue and field wages are Houston; plus minor citation and source_id fixes.

issues.current: For a Medicare-track skilled agency, request licensed home health services now and add licensed and certified home health services after CMS certification.
issues.correct: On the initial TULIP application request the 'licensed and certified home health services' category; HHSC issues an interim license showing 'licensed home health services' while CMS certification is pending and adds the certified category automatically when CMS certifies.
issues.evidence: 26 TAC §558.13(d): 'An applicant who has requested the category of licensed and certified home health services on the initial license application must also apply to CMS... (1) While the applicant is waiting for CMS to certify it... HHSC issues an initial license reflecting the category of licensed home health services... (2) If CMS certifies an agency... HHSC sends a notice to the agency that the category of licensed and certified home health services has been added.' The automatic add only applies to applicants who requested the L&C category initially; the checklist tells customers to request LHHS only.
issues.fix: Replace instructions with: 'For a Medicare-track agency, request the licensed and certified home health services category on the initial application. HHSC issues the license with the licensed home health services category while you wait for CMS, you must follow 42 CFR Part 484 as if certified, and HHSC adds the certified category when CMS certifies you (26 TAC §558.13(d)). Add PAS only if you will provide attendant care.'

issues.evidence: Same as checklist[6]: 26 TAC §558.13(d) ties the interim LHHS license and automatic addition of the certified category to having requested the L&C category on the initial application.
issues.fix: Reword recommendation 1 as shown in 'correct'; also align sections.executive_summary/service_model wording ('A skilled home health agency picks one of two categories').

issues.evidence: No published source exists for Texas MA home health rates (the bundle itself lists MA rates in not_claimed). The $173.37 is the Houston-adjusted Medicare FFS LUPA skilled-nursing per-visit amount (CR 14304 Table 3: SN $176.96 national) applied to all 7.5 MA visits of every discipline, including aide visits that Medicare itself pays at $80.12. AJMC (S56) says only that MA payment is 'typically less' than traditional Medicare and gives no rate. MA is ~40% of revenue in the default configuration: recomputing hha100_mixed at 90% census gives revenue $131,374 vs cost $121,500 (net $9,875, 7.5%); net falls to zero if the MA rate is $140.85/visit or lower (9,875 / (90 x 0.45 x 7.5) = $32.51 below $173.37). Profitability of the lead configuration depends on this unsourced number.
issues.fix: Unverifiable. Keep the rate only as an explicitly labeled assumption (not source S18, which supports the FFS per-visit amount, not MA payment), or move it to not_claimed. Add a downside configuration with MA at a lower assumed rate (e.g. 80% of $173.37 = $138.70) and state in financial_narrative that hha100_mixed breaks even at about $141 per MA visit.

issues.current: No HHCAHPS survey vendor line
issues.correct: Add opex line 'HHCAHPS approved survey vendor (mandatory for Medicare-certified HHAs with 60+ eligible patients/yr)', basis fixed, amount from vendor quote
issues.evidence: 42 CFR §484.245(b)(1)(iii)(B): 'An HHA must contract with an approved, independent HHCAHPS survey vendor to administer the HHCAHPS on its behalf.' Only HHAs with fewer than 60 eligible unique HHCAHPS patients can claim an exemption. At 25-100 active patients the agency exceeds 60 unique patients a year. Failing to report HH QRP data costs a 2-point lower update (CY 2026 $1,998.41 vs $2,038.22, CR 14304). SCHEMA rule 5 requires every mandatory cost the rules create.
issues.fix: Add the opex line with cite '42 CFR §484.245(b)' and a source_id for the regulation. The dollar amount is unverifiable (vendor pricing is not public), so label it an operator estimate pending quotes, and add a checklist item in the Medicare phase: 'Contract an approved HHCAHPS vendor before the first Medicare patient.'

issues.current: RN 3.2, LVN 3.0, PT 2.0, PTA 1.5, OT 1.0, SLP 0.25, aide 0.5, MSW 0.15 h (11.6 h total)
issues.evidence: Visit counts trace to MedPAC Table 8-4 (8.4 visits: SN 4.1, therapy 3.8, aide/MSS 0.5; verified), but the 1.25-1.5 hours per visit 'including documentation and drive' has no source_id. The result is burdened field labor of about $576 per patient-month, about $69 per visit. That is lean next to MedPAC's implied all-in cost per visit (2024 payment $245/visit at a 21.2% margin, so about $193). The 1.5 h figure also covers OASIS start-of-care and recert visits, which run longer. Hours have no paid non-productive time (orientation, case conferences, PTO) beyond the 10% benefits estimate.
issues.fix: Unverifiable. Label hours-per-visit as an operator assumption in each staffing note, or source it. Consider a sensitivity case at 2.0 h per visit; at 90 patients that adds about $17k/month of burdened labor and makes hha100_mixed unprofitable.

issues.evidence: The model prices Houston revenue (CBSA 26420 wage index) and Houston field wages, but uses the Texas statewide median for the administrator. BLS OEWS 2025 Medical and Health Services Managers (11-9111): Texas median $114,150 but Houston-Pasadena-The Woodlands median $124,400 (O*NET local wages page). The supervising nurse similarly uses the statewide RN 75th percentile ($50.53) while field RNs use the Houston median.
issues.fix: Either use Houston wages consistently (administrator $124,400; check the Houston RN 75th percentile for the DON) or state that leadership salaries are statewide medians. At $124,400 the hha100_mixed net margin drops by about $1,030/month (10,250 x 1.205 / 12).

issues.current: Built on a $13.00 average attendant wage

issues.evidence: HHSC rate hearing summary: the Legislature funded Rider 23 'to increase the base wage for attendants from $10.60/hr to $13/hr, increase the payroll costs, taxes, and benefits percentage to... 14% for services provided in non-facility settings, and increase the associated administrative rate by $0.24 per hour.' $13 x 1.14 / 4 = $3.71 attendant component, which matches the stated rate build.
